trust_decision.summary: Every lookup of a client-provided session id in the inherited plain-object `clients` record must be an own-property lookup, decided at five sites in packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/engine.ts (four in onMessage, one in onWebSocket) with a new safeGet() helper.

landing_point.why: The summary ('unsafe client session lookup') names the only session map in the monorepo, `clients`; the base engine.io verify() resolves `this.clients[sid]` there, and it is already guarded by hasOwn() at server.ts:310, so a reader starting from the report finds a fixed-looking base server and has to discover on their own that four other packages repeat the same lookup (the vulnerable copies are in packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/engine.ts).

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP polling request carrying ?sid= on a peer node: ClusterEngine.verify (engine.ts:427) publishes ACQUIRE_LOCK, which every node handles here; also reachable from the inter-node bus subscribed in redis.ts:147 and cluster.ts:48
client packet POSTed to a peer node's polling endpoint -> _hookTransport packet listener (engine.ts:475) -> _onPacket (engine.ts:526) -> PACKET message handled here
WebSocket upgrade probe on a peer node -> _onUpgradeSuccess (engine.ts:628) -> UPGRADE message handled here
transport error/close on a hooked transport (engine.ts:478-483) -> _onClose (engine.ts:538) -> CLOSE message handled here
GET /engine.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket&sid=... upgrade request (Server.handleUpgrade -> verify -> ws.handleUpgrade -> onWebSocket)

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Cross-node WebSocket takeover: a sid owned by another node must fall through the truthiness test at engine.ts:556 so the upgrade path can create a *new* local client for it (engine.ts:596, clientsCount++). A fix that rejects or closes any sid not already present in the local map, instead of only refusing inherited keys, breaks the 'should upgrade' / 'should upgrade and send buffered messages' flows.

O6_input_shapes: prototype member names such as __proto__ / constructor / toString, which resolve to inherited values on a plain-object map

a 20-character name that really exists on Object.prototype (e.g. propertyIsEnumerable), which passes the length-only isValidSessionId() gate at engine.ts:409 and so reaches the ACQUIRE_LOCK site through verify
the same sid string arriving inside an inter-node message payload (redis.ts:150 decode / cluster.ts:48 process message) rather than in a query string

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new message type (e.g. heartbeat/migrate) resolving its sid through this.clients instead of the Map used by DRAIN
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the DRAIN handler sits directly between the patched handlers and already resolves a sid-keyed session; the next message type a maintainer adds would copy that shape, and clients is the only sid-keyed store that is a plain object

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a session hand-off / restore path that reads or writes this.clients[sid] from a message payload without an own-property check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the takeover flow already writes this.clients[sid] = socket for a sid that came from another process, so an 'adopt/restore session' variant is a small, natural extension

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the uWebSockets.js HTTP path resolving a session by req._query.sid with no local guard (it leans on BaseServer.verify)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is a second HTTP implementation of the same lookup; a maintainer adding a pre-verify fast path there would index clients directly, exactly as the old cluster-engine code did

O9_family: unsafe object-key lookup / prototype-chain confusion in a client-controlled session map (CWE-20), reachable as a crash of the worker

O10_build.toolchain: npm; `npm run compile` = rimraf dist && tsc; `npm run test:unit` = mocha --import=tsx test/*.ts; prettier --check
services: redis (only for test/redis.ts; compose.yaml in packages/socket.io-cluster-engine)
O10_build.project_tests: packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/test/in-memory.ts (three engines on localhost ports 3000-3002 sharing an EventEmitter bus: read/write, locks, close, upgrade), test/cluster.ts (node cluster, 3 workers), test/redis.ts (needs a local Redis). No test covers prototype-named sids; the published fix adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Patch only the HTTP-facing check at engine.ts:556 (the path you can reproduce in a browser) or blacklist the names __proto__/constructor/toString, leaving the four onMessage lookups on the inherited map untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The inter-node bus accepts any message whose _source is the literal "_eio" (packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/redis.ts:50-58, lib/cluster.ts:48-53), so anyone able to publish on the Redis channel can forge cluster messages; noted only as the reachability path into onMessage and not pursued.
